question.problem:

Consider the functions ${y}_{1}(x)$ and ${y}_{2}(x)$ above. Given that ${y}_{1}$ and ${y}_{2}$ are solutions of the same second-order linear differential equation, select the correct options in the reasoning below.

question.worked_solution:
Suppose the functions ${y}_{1}(x)$ and ${y}_{2}(x)$ are defined on some interval $I.$
The Wronskian $W({y}_{1},{y}_{2})$ of these functions is defined as

$$
W({y}_{1},{y}_{2})=|\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & {y}_{2} \\ {y}_{1}^{′} & {y}_{2}^{′}\end{aligned}|={y}_{1}{y}_{2}^{′}-{y}_{2}{y}_{1}^{′}.
$$

Recall the following:

- If $W\ne 0$ for at least one $x\in I,$ then ${y}_{1}$ and ${y}_{2}$ are linearly independent.

- If $W=0$ and it’s known that ${y}_{1}$ and ${y}_{2}$ are solutions to the same second-order linear differential equation, then ${y}_{1}$ and ${y}_{2}$ are linearly dependent.

In our case, the Wronskian is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}W({y}_{1},{y}_{2}) & =|\begin{aligned}2{sin}^{2}⁡x & 1-{cos}^{2}⁡x \\ {(2{sin}^{2}⁡x)}^{′} & {(1-{cos}^{2}⁡x)}^{′}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2{sin}^{2}⁡x & 1-{cos}^{2}⁡x \\ 4\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x & 2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x\end{aligned}| \\  & =(2{sin}^{2}⁡x)(2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-(1-{cos}^{2}⁡x)(4\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\  & =4({sin}^{2}⁡x)(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-4({sin}^{2}⁡x)(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

which is $\text{zero for all }x\in R.$

Therefore, the set $\{{y}_{1}(x),{y}_{2}(x)\}$ is linearly $\text{dependent}$ on $R.$

choices.value: nonzero for at least one $x\in R$
